headline: AI Agents get deterministic name resolution to fix tool call hallucinations
summary: AI agents often fail when calling tools due to linguistic drift and hallucinated names. A new deterministic name resolution system, the Tool Namespace Resolver and Fuzzy Matcher, aims to eliminate these errors and improve reliability.
details: AI agents frequently struggle with tool calls, often hallucinating names or truncating identifiers. This linguistic drift causes 'Tool not found' errors in typical Model Context Protocol (MCP) implementations.

These failures result in inefficient loops, wasting tokens and risking the agent losing its original task context during retries. Building reliable autonomous systems requires more than just LLM schema adherence.

A solution involves a deterministic translation layer, specifically a Tool Namespace Resolver and Fuzzy Matcher. This system treats tool selection as a prioritized search problem rather than a binary check.
It implements a four-stage resolution hierarchy, moving beyond rigid equality checks towards probabilistic recognition handled by deterministic code. This approach mimics human ambiguity resolution.

The resolver offers three distinct entry points, providing granular control for various architectural needs, from single calls to massive instruction batches. Careful balancing of Levenshtein distance is crucial to prevent both collisions and ineffectiveness.

Enterprises integrate these agents with live CRMs and databases, making robust safety mechanisms essential. If an agent hallucinates a command similar to an administrative tool, a blindly correcting resolver could bypass primary safety.

Vinkius addresses this by providing governance policies like DLP and SSRF prevention at the protocol level. Its connectors, built with the open-source MCPFusion framework, run within isolated V8 sandboxes.

This unified gateway approach simplifies management, offering a single connection token for an entire suite of tools. It eliminates the complexity of configuring numerous OAuth callbacks and credentials for each utility script.

headline: AI security agent finds 24 Android vulnerabilities using open-source tool
summary: Researchers leveraged a new open-source AI security agent to uncover dozens of bugs across Android applications, detailing the targeted AI taskflows behind these findings.
details: A new open-source AI security agent has successfully identified 24 vulnerabilities in Android applications. This innovative tool employs targeted AI taskflows to systematically scan for potential security flaws.

The findings include various types of bugs, demonstrating the agent's effectiveness in uncovering hidden weaknesses. The project aims to provide developers with a powerful resource for enhancing app security.

The creators have released the agent as open source, allowing other developers and security researchers to utilize and contribute to its capabilities. Instructions are available for running the agent on individual applications.
This development highlights the growing role of AI in cybersecurity, offering automated methods to detect and mitigate vulnerabilities more efficiently than traditional manual reviews.
